交響樂團用弦樂、木管、銅管、打擊四家族分工；國樂團把同樣的四個位置換成吹管、彈撥: A symphony orchestra divides the work among four families — strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion; a Chinese orchestra puts the same four positions in the hands of winds, plucked strings, bowed strings and percussion. The correspondence is not tidy: the orchestra's middle layer is carried by the string section, while the Chinese orchestra hands it to a group of plucked instruments whose sound fades the instant they are plucked; the orchestra's bass is held up by double basses and cellos, while the Chinese orchestra has no ready-made bass instrument at all. Most of this line-up's history has gone into filling those two gaps.
交響樂團由弦樂群佔住的中聲部，在這裡由撥弦承擔；靠輪指、滾奏把短促的撥音接成長音: The middle register that the string section occupies in an orchestra is carried here by plucked strings; tremolo and rapid repeated strokes join the short plucked notes into long ones
低音是第三個、也是最難的問題。為了讓低音聽起來仍然「像國樂」，樂器製作者造出革胡: The bass is the third and hardest problem. To make the bass still sound like Chinese music, instrument makers built the gehu: a cello-sized body fitted with the skin vibration and movable bridge of an erhu, plus a double-bass gehu to take the bottom octave. The gehu answered the question of whose sound the bass belongs to, but brought new trouble — the membrane is sensitive to humidity, the strings are uneven in volume, the instrument is expensive and few people can repair it. Many orchestras therefore switch outright to cello and double bass. The choice is audible at once: the bass is wooden and round rather than the nasal tone of a skin, and the orchestra's top and bottom then come from two different acoustic worlds. Chinese orchestras in Hong Kong keep working on the gehu with substitute materials and redesigned structures, which shows the problem has never really been solved.
先聽低音。判斷低音是革胡、大提琴還是低音提琴：革胡帶著膜振動的鼻音，大提琴與低音: Start with the bass. Work out whether it is a gehu, a cello or a double bass: the gehu has the nasal tone of a vibrating skin, the cello and double bass a wooden roundness. This layer decides whether the whole orchestra sounds like Chinese instruments or like a symphony orchestra.
協調方式也變了。江南絲竹、廣東音樂這類傳統樂種沒有指揮，樂手靠聽鼓、聽領奏來對齊: The way the band is coordinated has changed too. Traditional genres such as Jiangnan sizhu and Guangdong music have no conductor; players line up by listening to the drum and to the lead. A Chinese orchestra is a conducted line-up: tempo, balance between sections, and how the plucked tremolo and the bowed bowing line up are all decided by the conductor, while the leader is responsible for tuning and for unified bowing. This is a structural change: music moves from a practice that can be negotiated to a full score handed out to the sections for execution.

吹管是穿透力最強的一層，嗩吶負責齊奏的亮度與高潮，笛負責線條與裝飾: The winds are the most penetrating layer: the suona carries the brightness and the climaxes of the tutti, the dizi the lines and the ornamentation
和北管、南管這類館閣相比，差別在有沒有總譜與指揮。北管與南管的編制、曲目與裝飾靠: Compared with the amateur halls of beiguan and nanguan, the difference is whether there is a full score and a conductor. Beiguan and nanguan keep their line-ups, repertoire and ornamentation alive by oral transmission and memory, and the number of players and instruments in a hall stays fairly fixed; a Chinese orchestra is a standardised organisation whose sections can be added to or cut for each piece, where players read parts and the conductor unifies tremolo and bowing.
國樂團是二十世紀的編制。阮、笙、嗩吶、笛都被擴充成高音到低音的家族，革胡更是為了: The Chinese orchestra is a twentieth-century line-up. The ruan, sheng, suona and dizi were all extended into families running from high to low, and the gehu was newly built to supply a bass; most of the repertoire is new work or arrangement, not old pieces as they were.
國樂團最基本的問題，是三個主要層次的持續能力對不上：彈撥一撥即衰，吹管能持續但受: The most basic problem of a Chinese orchestra is that its three main layers cannot sustain sound in the same way: a plucked note fades the moment it is plucked, a wind can sustain but only for the length of a breath, a bowed string can sustain but is quiet. The long tones an orchestra holds with a slab of strings have to be replaced here: plucked players repeat the same note fast in tremolo, which sounds like a line yet lets the pick's attack be heard at every point; the bowed strings make up volume by adding players. So when you hear a very long chord from a Chinese orchestra, it is usually not one instrument sustaining but many instruments sounding again at great speed.
國樂團演奏的是傳統國樂，樂器與古時候一樣。: A Chinese orchestra plays traditional Chinese music, on instruments the same as in old times.
國樂團的四個聲部，就等於交響樂團的四個家族。: The four sections of a Chinese orchestra are the same as the orchestra's four families.
國樂團（Chinese Orchestra）— 把傳統樂器按交響樂團方式分組、擴: Chinese Orchestra — a large ensemble that groups traditional instruments the way a symphony orchestra does, after extending their ranges. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
國樂團（Chinese orchestra）是把笛、笙、嗩吶、琵琶、二胡這批傳統: The Chinese orchestra is a large ensemble that regroups traditional instruments — dizi, sheng, suona, pipa, erhu — into four sections, winds, plucked strings, bowed strings and percussion, along the lines of a symphony orchestra. It did not grow out of any one existing tradition; it is the result of twentieth-century redesign, extension and standardisation, done so that these instruments could play multi-part music on a large scale. The name follows the region: guoyue in Taiwan, minzu guanxianyue in China, zhongyue in Hong Kong, huayue in Chinese communities in Singapore and Malaysia.
在台灣，國樂團出現在音樂廳、文化中心、校園巡演、節慶與廟會場合；生態包含公立職業: In Taiwan the Chinese orchestra appears in concert halls, cultural centres, school tours, festivals and temple fairs; the ecology runs from publicly funded professional orchestras to school classes and university clubs to community amateur groups, with a lot of movement between professional and amateur. In China, minzu guanxianyue orchestras are divided into national, provincial and municipal levels and conservatory ensembles, and the share of professional posts with state support is far higher. Hong Kong's Chinese orchestras are full-time professional bodies that treat instrument development and commissions for large symphonic works as part of their institutional task. Singapore's Chinese orchestras are professional; in Malaysia, huayue lives mainly in schools and societies.
對應並不對稱。交響樂團的中層是弦樂，國樂團交給撥弦；交響樂團的低音是弦樂家族的一: The correspondence is not symmetrical. An orchestra's middle layer is strings; a Chinese orchestra gives it to plucked strings. An orchestra's bass is a member of the string family; a Chinese orchestra has to borrow one or build one. That asymmetry is the signature of the Chinese orchestra's sound, and the thing most often criticised about it.
找現場演出。彈撥的起音、鼓的殘響與大廳的空間感，在錄音裡很容易被壓平。: Go and hear one live. The attack of the plucked strings, the decay of the drums and the sense of the hall are easily flattened in a recording.
拉弦家族是旋律的主力，音色接近人聲，但在大編制裡音量偏薄，必須靠數量與擴音補: The bowed family is the main carrier of melody, its timbre close to the human voice, but in a large line-up it is thin in volume and has to be made up with numbers and amplification
排鼓、堂鼓、大鑼、雲鑼、木魚、鈸: Paigu, tanggu, large gong, yunluo, wooden fish, cymbals
撐住和聲根音；這一層是整個編制最不穩定的部分: Holds the roots of the harmony; this layer is the least settled part of the whole line-up
收穫是音量、和聲的完整、以及演奏交響曲式、協奏曲、影視配樂與西方改編曲的能力。代: What is gained is volume, complete harmony, and the ability to play symphonic forms, concertos, film and TV scores and arrangements of Western music. What it costs is local intonation, the flexibility of ornamentation and improvisation, the individual timbre of each solo instrument, and the particular bowings and fingerings that carry a regional style.
曲目大致分幾類：民族管弦樂的大型作品（交響詩、組曲）、為二胡、琵琶、笛、嗩吶寫的: The repertoire falls into a few groups: large minzu guanxianyue works (symphonic poems, suites), concertos written for erhu, pipa, dizi or suona, arrangements of symphonies and operas, arrangements of regional genres (Jiangnan sizhu, Guangdong music, Chaozhou gong and drum), and film, TV and pop scores. Orchestras also often work with opera and folk singers, and in that role they are closer to an accompanying band than to the star of the concert.
最常被拿來對照的是管弦樂團。兩者都由指揮統籌、讀總譜、在音樂廳演出，但中層與低音: The usual comparison is the symphony orchestra. Both are run by a conductor, read a full score and perform in concert halls, but the middle layer and the bass come from different places: an orchestra's middle is a slab of strings sounding continuously under the bow, while a Chinese orchestra uses plucked strings and joins the decaying notes back into long ones with tremolo; an orchestra's bass belongs to the string family itself, while a Chinese orchestra has to build a gehu or simply borrow cello and double bass. The tuning reference differs too: an orchestra tunes to the oboe's A, a Chinese orchestra to the fixed pitches of the sheng and yangqin, and it uses equal temperament to flatten out the intonation of the regional genres.
柳琴、琵琶、中阮、大阮、揚琴、箏、三弦: Liuqin, pipa, zhongruan, daruan, yangqin, zheng, sanxian
梆笛、曲笛、新笛、高音笙、高音嗩吶: Bangdi, qudi, xindi, soprano sheng, soprano suona
標記段落、控制速度，也提供戲曲式的音響: Marks the sections, controls the tempo and supplies opera-style sonorities
每一族樂器都被拉成「高音—中音—低音」的家族，是這個編制的核心工程。阮從單一樂器: Pulling every family into high, middle and low versions is the central engineering of this line-up. The ruan went from a single instrument to xiaoruan, zhongruan, daruan and bass ruan; the sheng gained an alto and a bass, the bass sheng even taking a keyboard; the suona was extended downward into tenor and bass; the dizi gained the xindi and the large dadi. The aim is for one timbre to stack a complete chord by itself, without borrowing from another family every time. This turning of solo instruments into families is the main line of twentieth-century Chinese instrument reform.
聽吹管的穿透力。嗩吶一響會蓋過整團，這是編制設計的結果，不是失控；笛在同樣音量下: Listen to the penetration of the winds. One suona will cover the whole band — that is how the line-up is designed, not a loss of control; at the same volume the dizi has a finer timbre and more ornamentation.
聽彈撥怎麼代替弦樂。注意中阮與大阮的輪指：同一個音被快速反覆，聽起來像一條線，但: Listen to how the plucked strings stand in for strings. Notice the tremolo of the zhongruan and daruan: the same note repeated fast sounds like a line, yet the pick is audible at every point.
聽笙。笙是和聲的黏合劑，它把吹管與彈撥之間的縫隙填起來；注意它出現的時機，通常是: Listen to the sheng. It is the glue of the harmony, filling the gaps between winds and plucked strings; notice when it comes in — usually where the harmony needs sustaining.
與韓國國樂管弦樂團相比，兩者都是二十世紀把傳統樂器家族化、補上低音的設計，差別在: Compared with the Korean court-music orchestra, both are twentieth-century designs that turn traditional instruments into families and fill in the bass, and the difference is who holds the time. In the Korean orchestra, even with a conductor, the janggu remains the core of the rhythmic cycles and their landing points; in a Chinese orchestra the paigu and tanggu only mark sections, and the conductor decides tempo and alignment. The source material differs as well: the Korean orchestra has to fit two traditions of very different volume and timbre — court music and folk music — into one line-up, while the Chinese orchestra works with regional genres such as Jiangnan sizhu, Guangdong music and Chaozhou music.
革胡、低音革胡，或大提琴、低音提琴: Gehu, double-bass gehu, or cello and double bass
革胡是二十世紀中葉為了讓國樂團有「中國音色」的低音而設計的混合樂器，結合大提琴的: The gehu is a hybrid designed in the mid twentieth century so that the Chinese orchestra could have a bass with a Chinese sound; it combines a cello body with the skin vibration of the erhu. It was never adopted across the board, and many orchestras still use cello and double bass.
革胡是傳統樂器，只是比較少見。: The gehu is a traditional instrument, only a rare one.
音律是第二個問題。國樂團採十二平均律與固定音高，但形成它的地方樂種並不是這樣運作: Temperament is the second problem. The Chinese orchestra uses equal temperament and fixed pitches, but the regional genres that formed it do not work that way: Jiangnan sizhu tunes by ear, on evenly spaced fingerholes; the yifan mode of Guangdong music has its own intonation; the qingliu, zhongliu and huowu modes of Chaozhou music slide by microtones. Inside the orchestra all of this is flattened out. Because the sheng and yangqin can sound fixed pitches steadily, they become the tuning reference, and the bowed and plucked strings lean towards them. The result is unified intonation — and, along with it, a unified regional timbre.
